source.title: Deep Learning without Shortcuts: Shaping the Kernel with Tailored Rectifiers
source.authors: Guodong Zhang; Aleksandar Botev; James Martens

record.tranche_reason: Tests training accuracy of deep shortcut-free networks under different initialization methods; it does not measure the exact training-error comparisons in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Figure 7 reports ImageNet training accuracy for vanilla networks using TAT or EOC. The text describes their training accuracy as competitive, if not better, for EOC. Other reported validation-accuracy results do not measure training error and are omitted.
record.test_reason: Appendix E.4 directly compares training-accuracy trajectories under TAT and EOC, bearing on V4's initialization and training-speed claim. The authors explicitly attribute TAT's advantage to generalization rather than optimization. The networks lack batch normalization, and no residual-network training-error control is reported, so these rows do not test V3's stated comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate with qualification: TAT makes deep vanilla networks approach ResNet validation performance, with remaining gaps depending on depth, optimizer and training budget. Appendix E.4 attributes its advantage over EOC to generalization rather than optimization. Normalization-free rescaled residual networks can match or exceed standard ResNet validation accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses tailored activation transformation and compares it with EOC on ImageNet; does not reproduce the cited studies' recipes for the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and initialization method are varied in the training-accuracy comparison; the text does not quantify their effects there.

fits_no_version.finding: TAT improves validation accuracy and reduces its degradation with depth relative to EOC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tailored activation transformations improve generalization in deep vanilla networks; validation accuracy alone does not establish improved optimization or reduced training-error degradation.

fits_no_version.finding: TReLU has smaller empirical kernel-approximation errors, including under Gaussian initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation transformations affect initialization-time kernel fidelity; these measurements alone do not establish faster learning or greater trainable depth.

record.problems: The training-accuracy outcomes are presented in a figure without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The text gives only an aggregate qualitative comparison across settings.
record.rows_left_out: Validation-accuracy tables and plots were left out because they do not measure training error or training accuracy.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR-10/100 training classification error under SGD or Adam, including random or corrupted labels.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-related training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized networks versus identity-shortcut controls; the specific tanh and Fixup qualifications.

Maximum trainable depth; training-speed comparisons between variance-matched orthogonal and Gaussian tanh networks; 10,000-layer convolutional training. Table 11 reports final validation accuracy rather than these outcomes.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss transients, curvature trajectories and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: An aggregate comparison recording the authors' explicit finding that EOC training accuracy is competitive or better and that TReLU improves generalization rather than optimization. Existing rows contain no readable outcomes, although their notes mention this result.
missing.locator: Appendix E.4, Figure 7 and accompanying paragraph

record.verdict_notes: TAT changes the activation function as well as its initialization-time behavior, so this is not an isolated weight-initialization experiment. The result limits an extension of V4 to additional kernel shaping; it does not refute the benefits of preventing vanishing or exploding signals. Validation-only results were already declared in rows_left_out and are not missing training results.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100, corrupted or random labels, and near-zero training classification error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious local minima.

The study tests deep shortcut-free networks but does not report the plain-versus-shortcut comparison of training error, or the claimed depth-related training-error pattern. Its separate tanh and normalization-free residual-network claims are not tested here.
The paper compares initializations but does not report initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth as specified by this version.
Learning-rate stability threshold, curvature changes, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

relationships.condition: ImageNet vanilla ReLU-family networks, 50–200 layers, K-FAC, 90 epochs: TAT versus EOC
relationships.reason: Appendix E.4 explicitly says EOC achieves competitive or better training accuracy and attributes TAT's gains to generalization, qualifying the optimization benefit of additional kernel shaping. This is the text's aggregate interpretation of R1–R6; individual depth-specific differences are unreadable.
relationships.display_finding: EOC achieved competitive or better training accuracy, and the authors attributed TAT's gains to generalization.

source_check.condition: ImageNet vanilla ReLU-family networks, 50–200 layers, K-FAC, 90 epochs: TAT versus EOC
source_check.reason: R1–R6 and Appendix E.4 establish no optimization advantage from TAT over EOC. Both approaches use activation-matched initialization; V4 does not require further kernel shaping to improve on EOC. This result therefore does not demonstrate a condition where V4 fails or needs qualifying, and depth-specific effects cannot be read from the supplied text.

relation.reason: The study directly compares training accuracy under alternative initialization and activation-shaping methods, although this comparison does not establish a limitation of V4.

tranche.reason: TAT provides a different approach to initialization and activation shaping; Appendix E.4 compares training trajectories with EOC, addressing optimization in deep plain networks without reproducing the anchor recipes.

source_check.notes: Figure 7 supplies no numerical training-accuracy values in the extracted text; retaining figure-only values and cannot_determine states is appropriate. Stored excerpt E1 is tagged V3 despite its linked rows being V4; E.4 contains no residual-network training comparison.

statements.correction: Appendix E.4, Figure 7: ImageNet; vanilla networks; depths 50, 101 and 200; K-FAC; 90 epochs; hyperparameters selected by highest final validation accuracy. Authors report competitive or better EOC training accuracy and attribute TAT's advantage to generalization. No demonstrated failure of V4's stated initialization benefit.
statements.problem: The comparison and conditions are accurate, but its classification as evidence limiting V4 is unsupported. V4 does not predict that additional kernel shaping must outperform EOC, which already uses activation-matched initialization.
